chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from two men from our companions, who heard him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: 'Allah has not favored a servant with any blessing, so that he recognizes it in his heart and thanks Allah outwardly with his tongue, so that his speech is completed, until it is commanded for him to be given more.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for receiving an increase in blessings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanism of divine gratitude by linking internal recognition (shukr al-qalb) with verbal affirmation (shukr al-lisan), a concept central to Shia ethical theology. This dual expression of thankfulness is presented as the condition for 'tamam al-kalam' (completeness of praise), which triggers the divine promise of incremental increase (ziyadah) in blessings, reflecting the principle that gratitude is both a cause and a manifestation of divine favor.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from two men from our companions who both heard,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has not Favoured upon a servant from Bounties, so he recognises it in his heart and Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> apparently by his tongue, so he completes his speech, until He<sup>azwj</sup> Commands for the increase to be for him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from two men of our people who have said the following: “We heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘

If upon Allah’s granting a favor to a servant he acknowledges it in his heart, and expresses thanks to Him in public, as soon as his words are completed, an order is issued to give the servant more.’”
